alex: Heads-up — ran a 2h perf sweep on the reranker/embedding endpoint (non-chat) and saw a steady tail-latency increase after the kernel selector flip. probly affects short multi-candidate requests. :thinking:

maria: Ugh. Seen anything in KV cache metrics? sounds like prefix/KV eviction thrash if batches re-order.

alex: KV hit-rate dropped ~18% around the same time. CPU on worker pinned, but GPU utilization unchanged. stack suggests extra mem copies in the int8 kernel path.

sam: can you paste the perf snapshot? small notes: our continuous-batching heuristics try to keep token-budget per-batch ~128k tokens, but rerank requests are many tiny seqs so they get merged unpredictably.

alex: paste from the run: ```
# sample profile
requests: 14k
mean_latency_ms: 46
p95_ms: 210 -> observed regression
kv_hit_rate: 62% -> 44% after flip
kernel: auto-picked int8_avx_fast
copy_overhead_ms: +5-10 per batch
```

kevin: bench-bot results attached. bench-bot: "vector-rank-flow v3: earlyfill disabled; queue depth=256; avg batch size 9 -> p95 202ms"

julia: interesting — earlyfill was disabled during the canary to reduce too-small batches. for rerank/embeds we probably need a different policy: prioritize request-count fairness vs token budget.

maria: proposal: add a small policy tweak: for non-chat vector endpoints treat token budget not as hard target but as soft ceiling; add a min-request-count threshold (min_reqs=8) and prefer filling by count for sequences <64 tokens. should avoid tiny many-candidate batches.

sam: agreed. also add a kernel-selection guard: prefer fp16 kernel if batch contains >N short sequences because int8 path shows extra copy for packing. we can add a simple heuristic: if mean_seq_len < 64 and mean_batch_size > 6 -> prefer fp16.

kevin: ran a quick sim with those heuristics on staging: p95 down from 202ms to 138ms, kv_hit restored to ~60%. results: fewer evictions, smaller copy spikes.

alex: put the staging config snippet here so eng-infra can prod it tomorrow: ```json
{
  "queue_policy": "count_priority",
  "min_reqs": 8,
  "token_budget_target": 128000,
  "token_budget_mode": "soft_ceiling",
  "kernel_guard": {
    "int8_prefer": false,
    "fp16_bias_threshold_seq_len": 64,
    "fp16_min_batch_size": 6
  }
}
```

julia: looks fine. add a short-circuit to bypass KV cache evictions: if batch will rebuild >50% new KV entries, mark as no_eviction window to keep hot keys.

maria: can we metricize this quickly? add a tag on requests that hit the count_priority path and track p50/p95 + kv_hit. will help rollback decisions.

profile-bot: profile uploaded -> s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1882233445/vector-tokenflow-v3.pb.gz :eyes:

alex: cool. I'm going to roll the config to staging at 02:00 UTC, run 1h smoke with real traffic, then schedule a 30m canary to prod if p95 holds. tagging @sam @kevin for on-call during the roll. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll watch the kernel selector logs and the copy metrics. if we see any regression we flip kernel bias back and revert queue policy.

kevin: I'll automate the metric dashboard for the count_priority tag and set an alert on p95 spike > +30%.

maria: thanks team. follow-up tomorrow to see post-canary profile and decide if we should bake this into default rerank policy. :coffee:
